The protein content of this product meets my nutritional needs.
The flavor varieties offered are appealing to me.
I would purchase this smoothie as a healthy meal replacement option.

example.respondent_instruction_for_concept: View the concept (image) and rate the following statements based on your first impression. Use only the info shown. No right or wrong answers.

survey_editable_lines.1: You are tasked with answering a conjoint survey question related to examining factors that influence purchase of facial moisturizer as the following individual:
survey_editable_lines.10:
Before selecting an option, consider the following:
1. Consider how your demographic traits and lifestyle influence your priorities for the decision.
2. Evaluate the options in the survey question based on these priorities.
survey_editable_lines.12: Please read the descriptions of facial moisturizers (50ml) carefully. Then, please select which facial moisturizer you would purchase.
survey_editable_lines.4: Imagine you are in a situation where You need to purchase a facial moisturizer for your daily skincare routine from an online retailer that provides detailed product specifications.
survey_editable_lines.5: - Consider the different combinations of factors and select the option that would most likely lead to the maximize level of purchase of facial moisturizer.
survey_editable_lines.6: - When evaluating each option, consider how the combination of factors would realistically interact to affect purchase of facial moisturizer.
survey_editable_lines.7: - Choose the scenario where the presented conditions would be most conducive to maximizing purchase of facial moisturizer.
survey_editable_lines.9: Answer the survey question as this person, following these steps:

example.why_prompt: What are the key factors influencing consumers' purchase consideration and preference for upgrading their mobile devices, such as from an iPhone 12 to an iPhone 15 or Samsung Galaxy S22 to S24?

add_neither_option.description: Append a 'None of these' opt-out row to every choice task. Default true. Replication mode defaults it to false unless the payload sends it.
add_neither_option.title: Add Neither Option

additional_notes_max_workers.description: Parallel model calls for additional notes. Default 100. Operator knob; leave unset.
additional_notes_max_workers.title: Additional Notes Max Workers

alternative_shuffle_seed.description: Seed for the order profiles appear within each choice task. Default 10000.
alternative_shuffle_seed.title: Alternative Shuffle Seed

alternatives_per_task.description: Number of profiles shown per choice task. None (default): today's behaviour — the attribute-count heuristic, or 2 when binary_choice is true. Set 2..6 to show exactly that many profiles (the opt-out row, when add_neither_option is true, is added on top). The run summary reports both the requested and the realized count. Single-profile rating tasks (1) are not supported yet.
alternatives_per_task.title: Alternatives Per Task

attribute_count.description: Attributes to generate when the engine builds the design, 2 to 10. Default 8. Ignored with pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.
attribute_count.title: Attribute Count

attribute_shuffle_seed.description: Seed for the order attributes appear in each profile. Default 1000. With design_seed, price_generation_seed and alternative_shuffle_seed it fixes the realized survey.
attribute_shuffle_seed.title: Attribute Shuffle Seed

batch_size.description: Respondents per model batch in the survey step. Default 20. Operator knob; leave unset.
batch_size.title: Batch Size

binary_choice.description: Show exactly two profiles per choice task. Default false uses the attribute-count heuristic. alternatives_per_task overrides both.
binary_choice.title: Binary Choice

block_optimization_iteration_limit.description: Iterations the block optimizer spends balancing choice tasks across respondents. Default 100 on dev, 200 elsewhere. Operator knob; leave unset.
block_optimization_iteration_limit.title: Block Optimization Iteration Limit

check_for_continuous_variables.description: Applies to engine-generated designs only. When `pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup` is supplied, submitted levels are used exactly as sent and this flag has no effect (#2074, #2396): the engine never reclassifies a submitted level as continuous or draws replacement values.
check_for_continuous_variables.title: Check For Continuous Variables

concept_description.description: Text description of the concept for concept_testing, used with or instead of an image.
concept_description.title: Concept Description

concept_heading.description: Heading the worker composes for a concept_testing run from the concept description, image and statements. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
concept_heading.title: Concept Heading

concept_statements.description: Statements respondents rate in concept_testing, each {statement, labels} where labels is the ordered rating scale.
concept_statements.title: Concept Statements

confidence_level.description: Low, Medium or High, derived from model fit. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
confidence_level.title: Confidence Level

conjoint_time.description: Minutes the survey stage took. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
conjoint_time.title: Conjoint Time

context.description: Study context shown to respondents ahead of the choice tasks. Empty (default) lets the worker derive it from why_prompt.
context.title: Context

cost_amount.description: Model cost of the run in USD. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
cost_amount.title: Cost Amount

country.description: Country of the respondent population and design context. Default 'United States'. Other countries need non_us_target_population.
country.title: Country

coverage_probability.description: Reserved; currently always 0. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
coverage_probability.title: Coverage Probability

dcm_survey_workers.description: Parallel model calls for the survey step, capped at the task count. Default 128. Operator knob; leave unset.
dcm_survey_workers.title: Dcm Survey Workers

decision_time_seed.description: Not read by the worker; kept for payload compatibility.
decision_time_seed.title: Decision Time Seed

design_seed.description: Feature flag. None (default): today's behaviour — a fresh randomized design every run. Set an integer to make the realized design (choice tasks, level shuffles, Sobol scramble) a pure function of the seed, so two runs of one configuration are true replicates and A/B comparisons can be paired. Defaulting this on waits on the #2149 review.
design_seed.title: Design Seed

deterministic_stages.description: When true, the pre-survey LLM stages (latent-variable generation and scoring, persona bios, mood statements, decision strategy) run at llm_temperature instead of their fixed 0.7, so a rerun with the same seeds reproduces the same respondent prompts. Default false keeps today's behaviour.
deterministic_stages.title: Deterministic Stages

do_research.description: Run a background GPT Researcher pass on why_prompt alongside the study and attach its report to the run. Default false. Forced false in replication mode and skipped for human-baseline runs.
do_research.title: Do Research

dv_llm_model.description: Model that phrases the dependent variable (the choice question) from why_prompt. Not used when respondent_dependent_variable is supplied. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

effect_encoding.description: Effects-code attribute levels (sum to zero) in the utility model instead of dummy coding. Default true.
effect_encoding.title: Effect Encoding

ensure_25_trait_level_count.description: Grow the sample until every trait level has at least 25 respondents. Default false.
ensure_25_trait_level_count.title: Ensure 25 Trait Level Count

estimation_method.description: Utility estimation. HB (default): hierarchical Bayes mixed logit with individual-level utilities. MLE: a single multinomial logit.
estimation_method.title: Estimation Method

experiment_type.description: conjoint (default) runs a discrete choice experiment over attributes and levels. concept_testing shows a concept (image or description) and asks respondents to rate concept_statements.
experiment_type.title: Experiment Type

expr_llm_model.description: Model that answers the survey as each respondent. Default is the Databricks-served Claude Sonnet 3.7.

external_personas.description: LinkedIn profile URLs to build respondents from when use_external_personas is true.
external_personas.title: External Personas

generate_additional_notes.description: Ask the model for free-text notes per respondent during latent-variable scoring. Default false.
generate_additional_notes.title: Generate Additional Notes

hb_folder.description: Legacy human-baseline path, now owned by Ditto: storage folder of a stored study to replicate. Only one of hb_folder and hb_run_id may be set. Prefer replication_mode with pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.
hb_folder.title: Hb Folder

hb_run_id.description: Legacy human-baseline path, now owned by Ditto: W&B run id of a stored study to replicate. Only one of hb_folder and hb_run_id may be set.
hb_run_id.title: Hb Run Id

image_name1.description: Uploaded image file name of the first concept for concept_testing. With image_name2 the run compares two concepts.
image_name1.title: Image Name1

image_name2.description: Uploaded image file name of the second concept for concept_testing. Leave empty to test one concept.
image_name2.title: Image Name2

include_price_brand.description: Ask the design generator to include price and brand attributes. Default false. Engine-generated designs only.
include_price_brand.title: Include Price Brand

is_hb_run.description: Legacy: marks the run as a human-baseline replication, which skips do_research and enables the hb_folder / hb_run_id sourcing. Default false.
is_hb_run.title: Is Hb Run

is_private.description: Restrict run visibility to its owner. Default false.
is_private.title: Is Private

latent_variables.description: Generate, score and paste the latent-variable (attitudinal) battery into every respondent prompt. Default true. Forced false in replication mode. See latent_variables_from_run to reuse a previous bundle instead of generating one.
latent_variables.title: Latent Variables

latent_variables_from_run.description: Reuse the latent-variable bundle (variable names, statements and every respondent's scores) of a previous run instead of generating a new one. Give the previous run's name (artifact experiment_latent_variables_<name>) or a local JSON path. Requires the same population. Default None generates a fresh bundle, as today.
latent_variables_from_run.title: Latent Variables From Run

latent_variables_llm_model.description: Model that generates the latent-variable battery (variable names). Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

latent_variables_scale_labels_count.description: Points on the rating scale used to score each statement. Default 5.
latent_variables_scale_labels_count.title: Latent Variables Scale Labels Count

latent_variables_traits_count.description: How many latent variables the battery generates. Default 4.
latent_variables_traits_count.title: Latent Variables Traits Count

level_count.description: Levels per generated attribute, 2 to 10. Default 5. Ignored with pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.
level_count.title: Level Count

levels_llm_model.description: Model that generates attributes and levels from why_prompt. Not used when pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup is supplied. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

levels_per_trait.description: Legacy: levels per trait when personas are generated through the traits API (use_api). Default 100.
levels_per_trait.title: Levels Per Trait

llm_temperature.description: Sampling temperature of the respondent survey step. Default 0.0: randomness here is measurement noise, not respondent heterogeneity. The pre-survey stages keep their fixed 0.7 unless deterministic_stages is true.
llm_temperature.title: Llm Temperature

lv_based_nl_summary_max_workers.description: Parallel model calls for the latent-variable summaries pasted into respondent prompts. Default 100. Operator knob; leave unset.
lv_based_nl_summary_max_workers.title: Lv Based Nl Summary Max Workers

lv_statement_llm_model.description: Model that writes the Likert statements for each latent variable. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

lv_statement_max_workers.description: Parallel model calls for latent-variable statements. Default 100. Operator knob; leave unset.
lv_statement_max_workers.title: Lv Statement Max Workers

match_population_distribution.description: Resample so the respondent mix matches the target population's distribution on the constrained demographics. Default false.
match_population_distribution.title: Match Population Distribution

match_population_distribution_concept.description: Concept-testing counterpart of match_population_distribution. Default true.
match_population_distribution_concept.title: Match Population Distribution Concept

max_length.description: Length limit passed to the attribute and level generator for each label. Default 40. Engine-generated designs only.
max_length.title: Max Length

mnp_model.description: Estimate with the multinomial probit (MNP) model; false uses multinomial logit (MNL). Default true.
mnp_model.title: Mnp Model

mood_statement_seed.description: Seed for assigning mood statements to respondents. Default 178942. Replication mode injects no mood.
mood_statement_seed.title: Mood Statement Seed

non_us_target_population.description: Constraints for a non-US population, passed as a free-form dict to the population builder. Cannot be combined with target_population or population_preset.
non_us_target_population.title: Non Us Target Population

null_levels.description: When true, every attribute gains an injected `Not available` level. Callers whose design must contain only the submitted levels must send `null_levels=false` explicitly; the default injects it.
null_levels.title: Null Levels

optimization_context.description: What the decision maker is optimizing, appended to target_behavior in the decision context. Empty (default) lets the worker derive it from why_prompt.
optimization_context.title: Optimization Context

paper_data.description: Rows of the source paper's reported results for human-baseline comparison; the worker reads the regression_model entry. Default empty.
paper_data.title: Paper Data

persona_nl_llm_model.description: Model that writes each respondent's natural-language bio from its demographic and trait record. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

persona_nl_workers.description: Parallel model calls for respondent bios, capped at the respondent count. Default 128. Operator knob; leave unset.
persona_nl_workers.title: Persona Nl Workers

population_group.description: Named segment to draw from when use_population_group is true.

population_preset.description: Name a stored US population instead of writing target_population by hand. us_general_adults resolves to age 18 to 99 across the twelve representative states the worker uses when no state is given, so a request that only carries population_traits can still queue. Cannot be combined with an explicit target_population constraint, non_us_target_population, use_nrg_population, use_external_personas, use_population_group or user_uploaded_persona; the request would then be describing the population twice, and is rejected with 422.

population_seed.description: Seed for the respondent draw. Identical configurations draw identical respondents unless resample_population is true. Default 100.
population_seed.title: Population Seed

population_traits.description: Modeled traits added uniformly to every respondent, keyed by trait name with a value or list of allowed values. Traits never select respondents: pair them with target_population or population_preset.

pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.description: Closed-world design: `[[attribute, [level, ...]], ...]`. Submitted levels are used exactly as sent, including numeric-looking and currency levels; the engine never reclassifies them as continuous or synthesises replacement prices (#2074, #2324). The only level that can be added is `Not available`, controlled by `null_levels`. Leave empty to have the engine generate the design from `why_prompt`.
pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.title: Pre Cooked Attributes And Levels Lookup

predict_trait_workers.description: Parallel model calls for trait prediction, capped at the respondent count. Default 128. Operator knob; leave unset.
predict_trait_workers.title: Predict Trait Workers

price_generation_seed.description: Seed for synthesized price levels when the engine generates the design. No effect with pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup. Default 1000.
price_generation_seed.title: Price Generation Seed

priority.description: Which worker tier runs this study. `high` routes to the `high_priority` queue and `default` to the `default` queue; each has its own dedicated worker, so `high` never queues behind `default` and `default` is never starved. Omitted requests get `high`. Note this replaces an older server-side inference from `hb_run_id`: a replication sourced by W&B run id used to be routed to `default` automatically and now is not, so send `"default"` explicitly if that is what you want.
priority.title: Priority

prob_to_discrete_seed.description: Seed for converting probabilistic responses to a single choice when response_type is probabilistic. Default 500.
prob_to_discrete_seed.title: Prob To Discrete Seed

prompt_type.description: How the design generator frames why_prompt: generic (default), product ('when purchasing') or service ('when choosing options for this service').
prompt_type.title: Prompt Type

r_analytics_time.description: Minutes the R analytics stage took. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
r_analytics_time.title: R Analytics Time

r_squared.description: Model fit as a whole-number percentage. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
r_squared.title: R Squared

realworld_products.description: Brand and product combinations behind a Product attribute. Engine-generated designs fill this from why_prompt. With pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup, more than one entry adds an always-available Product attribute. Default empty.
realworld_products.title: Realworld Products

replication_mode.description: Run the supplied study definition verbatim and refuse to improve it. Requires respondent_dependent_variable, which is used unchanged; add_neither_option defaults to false unless sent explicitly; no attitudinal battery or latent-variable scoring; no mood, decision-strategy, fatigue, price or second-best rules reach the respondent prompt. Use for replicating a published study. Default false.
replication_mode.title: Replication Mode

resample_population.description: Feature flag. False (default): the respondent sample is a pure function of population_seed — identical configs draw identical respondents, so runs are true replicates. True: restore the pre-2026-08-30 behaviour of drawing a fresh random sample every run (runs shared only 1.6-3.4% of respondents, the largest single source of run-to-run AMCE variance).
resample_population.title: Resample Population

respondent_dependent_variable.description: The choice question shown to respondents, used verbatim when supplied. Empty (default) lets dv_llm_model phrase it from why_prompt. Required in replication mode.
respondent_dependent_variable.title: Respondent Dependent Variable

respondent_instruction_for_concept.description: Instruction shown to respondents before they rate the concept in concept_testing.
respondent_instruction_for_concept.title: Respondent Instruction For Concept

respondent_instructions_preamble.description: Text placed before the choice question in every respondent prompt. Empty by default.
respondent_instructions_preamble.title: Respondent Instructions Preamble

response_contract.description: How respondents answer the survey step. cot_json (default) is today's contract: chain-of-thought inside a JSON object per task. short is the trimmed template with at most two sentences of reasoning per task and one final JSON line of choices; about 60% fewer output tokens.
response_contract.title: Response Contract

response_type.description: discrete (default): each respondent picks one profile per task. probabilistic: the respondent gives a probability per profile, converted to a choice with prob_to_discrete_seed.

sample_size.description: Respondents actually surveyed. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
sample_size.title: Sample Size

score_llm_model.description: Model that scores each respondent on the latent-variable statements. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

spearman_correlation.description: Reserved for the Spearman correlation of feature importance; currently always 0. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
spearman_correlation.title: Spearman Correlation

state.description: US state to restrict the population to; also settable inside target_population. None draws from twelve representative states.
state.title: State

survey_design_filelink.description: Storage key of an uploaded survey design parquet (survey-design/<uuid>.parquet). When set, that design is used instead of generating one.
survey_design_filelink.title: Survey Design Filelink

survey_editable_lines.description: Line-level overrides of the survey prompt template keyed by line number, as produced by the Holodeck prompt editor. Empty by default.
survey_editable_lines.title: Survey Editable Lines

Respondent Instructions:
You are answering questions as if you are a human. Do not break character.

Currently living in {state}, {country}, Time of Survey: year: {year}.

{options}

survey_prompt.description: Survey prompt template. Defaults to the built-in template; override only for prompt experiments. survey_editable_lines patches single lines instead.
survey_prompt.title: Survey Prompt

target_behavior.description: The behavior under study, for example 'choose a mobile phone to upgrade to'. Empty (default) lets the worker derive it from why_prompt.
target_behavior.title: Target Behavior

target_behavior_context.description: Set true by the worker when a study context was derived from why_prompt. Ignored on input.
target_behavior_context.title: Target Behavior Context

target_population.description: Demographic constraints that select US respondents. age and household_income are inclusive [low, high] ranges; the other keys are allowed-value lists. At least one constraint is required unless another population mode or population_preset is used. Omitting state draws from twelve representative states.

tasks_per_respondent.description: Choice tasks each respondent answered. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
tasks_per_respondent.title: Tasks Per Respondent

title.description: Display name of the run. Empty (default) lets the worker derive one from why_prompt.
title.title: Title

token_count.description: Model tokens consumed by the run. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
token_count.title: Token Count

total_number_of_tasks.description: Choice tasks in the realized design. Written by the worker into the run summary; ignored on input.
total_number_of_tasks.title: Total Number Of Tasks

trait_prediction_llm_model.description: Model that predicts each respondent's values for the modeled population_traits. Default Databricks Claude Sonnet 3.7.

use_api.description: Legacy switch for how trait personas are generated on the linear-schema path (API generator when true). Default true. Operator knob; leave unset.
use_api.title: Use Api

use_batching.description: Not read by the worker; kept for payload compatibility. Respondent batching is always on.
use_batching.title: Use Batching

use_external_personas.description: Population mode: build respondents from the LinkedIn profile URLs in external_personas. Exactly one population mode may be set.
use_external_personas.title: Use External Personas

use_halton_draws.description: Fill an under-sized orthogonal array with Halton draws instead of Sobol. Default false. Engine-generated designs only.
use_halton_draws.title: Use Halton Draws

use_multiprocessing.description: Not read by the worker; kept for payload compatibility.
use_multiprocessing.title: Use Multiprocessing

use_population_group.description: Population mode: draw respondents from the named segment in population_group. Exactly one population mode may be set.
use_population_group.title: Use Population Group

use_preassigned_blocks.description: Assign choice tasks from the Block column of an uploaded respondent file; falls back to random blocks when the column is absent. Default false.
use_preassigned_blocks.title: Use Preassigned Blocks

use_threading.description: Not read by the worker; kept for payload compatibility.
use_threading.title: Use Threading

user_uploaded_persona.description: Population mode: survey the respondents in the file at user_uploaded_persona_filelink instead of the synthetic population. Exactly one population mode may be set.
user_uploaded_persona.title: User Uploaded Persona

user_uploaded_persona_filelink.description: Storage key of the uploaded respondent parquet (population/<uuid>.parquet). Required when user_uploaded_persona is true.
user_uploaded_persona_filelink.title: User Uploaded Persona Filelink

why_prompt.description: The research question. Every generated part of the study (attributes, levels, dependent variable, context) is derived from it. Required.
why_prompt.title: Why Prompt

year.description: Time context given to the design generator and respondents. Defaults to the current month and year.
year.title: Year

queue_name.description: The queue this study was actually enqueued on, so the caller can see where their work went rather than inferring it from the `priority` they sent. Null when the experiment ran inline (DEBUG mode) or when the request failed before dispatch.
queue_name.title: Queue Name

LLMModel.description: Enum representing the llm model types used in the experiments.
LLMModel.title: LLMModel

PopulationPreset.description:
Named US populations a caller can select instead of spelling out
demographic constraints. Each resolves to a TargetPopulation with at least
one real constraint, so the run takes the bounded marginals-then-sample
path every constrained run takes (see Prepare_Population's guard on an
all-empty target, which exists because an unconstrained run fans out over
the whole frame until the worker is killed).
PopulationPreset.title: PopulationPreset

age.description: Inclusive [low, high] age range in years, for example [18, 65].
age.title: Age

education_level.description: Allowed education levels; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.
education_level.title: Education Level

gender.description: Allowed genders; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.
gender.title: Gender

household_income.description: Inclusive [low, high] annual household income range in USD.

number_of_children.description: Allowed number-of-children buckets; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.
number_of_children.title: Number Of Children

racial_group.description: Allowed racial groups; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.
racial_group.title: Racial Group

info.description:
💕SuperEgo API powers Consulting and Product teams to design and run cost-effective, ethical, causal experiments. 🚀 Generative AI for Experimental Design. 👨‍🔬⚗️

**Authentication.** Every endpoint takes a bearer token. post.description:
Starts an experiment asynchronously and returns a W&B run id to poll.

Supply the research question and a supported population selection, then
review the design, response and reproducibility options in the request
schema. The REST Experiment model and MCP's typed `advanced` object are
different contracts; not every REST option is exposed through MCP or the
browser form.

**Poll the returned run identity.** Normal execution queues the run;
debug mode can execute inline. A definite submission rejection returns
an error. Keep polling `in-queue`, `running` and `unknown`; a missing W&B
record or timed-out read is not a reason to submit another experiment.
REST does not provide the MCP launch-idempotency protocol. For a failed
or ambiguous launch, reconcile the original run before retrying.

**`population_traits` do not select a population.** Traits add modeled
attributes to respondents who were already selected by
`target_population` (or another population mode). A request that sends
`population_traits` with an empty or absent `target_population` is
rejected with `422` before anything is queued or any model is called; the
error names the missing constraint (for example `age`, `gender`,
`household_income`, `education_level`, `racial_group`,
`number_of_children`, or `state`).

**`check_for_continuous_variables` only affects engine-generated
designs.** When `pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup` is supplied,
the submitted levels are used exactly as sent and the flag has no
effect: nothing is reclassified as continuous and no replacement values
are drawn. Omit the levels to let the engine generate the design if
continuous inference is wanted.

**`population_preset` is a stored population.** Send
`population_preset: us_general_adults` instead of writing
`target_population` by hand; it expands to adults aged 18 to 99 across the
twelve representative states. It may carry `population_traits`, but a
preset next to `target_population`, `non_us_target_population`,
`use_population_group`, `use_external_personas`, `use_nrg_population` or
`user_uploaded_persona` is rejected with `422`, and an unknown preset name
is rejected by schema validation.

example.why_prompt: What factors drive consumer choice of electric vehicles?

get.description:
Get all the user runs/experiments.

Note: This endpoint may take time for users with many experiments.
Consider implementing pagination or caching for better performance.

schema.title: Response Get All User Runs Api V1 Runs All Get

delete.description:
Delete an experiment run by ID.

Args:
    run_id (str): The unique identifier of the run to delete.

Returns:
    Response: Empty response with 204 status code on successful deletion.

Raises:
    HTTPException: For various error scenarios including unauthorized access, not found, or server errors.

get.description:
Fetch details of a specific experiment run.

Parameters:
- `run_id`: Unique identifier of the run.

Returns:
JSONResponse with:
- `run_details`: Details of the requested run

Notes:
- Returns 403 if the run is private and not accessible to the user
- Returns 404 (not 500) while the run has no W&B record yet, with a
  `retryable` flag and a `Retry-After` header when the run is still live

Raises:
- HTTPException 404: If W&B has no record of the run
- HTTPException 500: If fetching run details fails

Returns the current state of a run.

**A terminal state is only reported with positive evidence.** The status
is resolved from the W&B run and then the Redis enqueue-time run-state
record. SQS has no result backend. A run that neither store knows
about is reported as `unknown`, which is never terminal. Absence is not
failure: a run is invisible to W&B for the whole window between
submission and the creation of its W&B run, queue wait included.

Normalised states are `in-queue`, `running`, `unknown`, `finished`,
`failed`, `crashed`, `killed`, and `lost`. A run is terminal in every
state except `in-queue`, `running`, and `unknown`.

`lost` now means one specific thing: a submitted run whose record never
reached a terminal state and is older than the six-hour grace window.
A queued or running record within that window remains non-terminal.

**Do not resubmit on a non-terminal status.** `in-queue`, `running`, and
`unknown` all mean "keep polling". Resubmitting multiplies server-side
runs of several hundred simulated respondents each.

**Still true of `finished`:** a run can finish having produced no
artifacts. A W&B `state` of `finished` whose `summary.status` is `failed`
is reported here as `failed`, but check `logged_artifacts()` before
treating a `finished` run as usable.

Returns the catalogue of persona traits. Review the trait descriptions
and level labels before building an experiment's `population_traits`
dictionary. That dictionary maps trait names to modeled values; a
catalogue ID alone is not a population-selection constraint.
